sub_criteria.name: baseline recall ceiling
sub_criteria.text: Reports or measures the recall/precision ceiling of single-query database search (BM25, embedding search, or a search API) as a comparison point.

sub_criteria.name: agentic mechanism gain
sub_criteria.text: Attributes a measured gain to a specific agentic move — query reformulation, citation-graph traversal, or iterative crawling — rather than to the system as an undifferentiated whole.

sub_criteria.name: retrieval/reranking method
sub_criteria.text: Describes or evaluates a retrieval or reranking technique underlying an agentic literature-search system (dense retrieval, learned reranker, hybrid search).

sub_criteria.name: benchmark construction
sub_criteria.text: Explains how an evaluation set for literature-search agents was built — query source, relevance labeling, corpus coverage, contamination controls.

sub_criteria.name: gain replication failure
sub_criteria.text: Shows a reported agentic gain shrinking, disappearing, or failing to generalize under a different benchmark, metric, or independent replication.

items.abstract_600: AIOps algorithms playa crucial role in the mainte-nance of microservice systems. Many previous benchmarks' per-formance leaderboard provides valuable guidance for selecting appropriate algorithms. However, existing AIOps benchmarks mainly utilize offline static datasets to evaluate algorithms. They cannot consistently evaluate the performance of algorithms using real-time datasets, and the operation scenarios for evaluation are static, which is insufficient for effective algorithm selection. To address these issues, we propose an evaluation-consistent and scenario-oriented evaluation framework

Can Generative AI improve social science?
items.abstract_600: Generative AI that can produce realistic text, images, and other human-like outputs is currently transforming many different industries. Yet it is not yet known how such tools might influence social science research. I argue Generative AI has the potential to improve survey research, online experiments, automated content analyses, agent-based models, and other techniques commonly used to study human behavior. In the second section of this article, I discuss the many limitations of Generative. I examine how bias in the data used to train these tools can negatively impact social science research

items.abstract_600: The rapid advancement of mobile applications has led to a significant demand for cross-platform compatibility, particularly between the Android and iOS platforms. items.abstract_600: Natural language processing (NLP) tools have been applied successfully in improving predictions in a wide range of research areas. However, what works in one area may not work in conflict research. This paper therefore seeks to offer an initial assessment of the most prominent NLP methods for conflict prediction tasks. items.title: ReXrank: A Public Leaderboard for AI-Powered Radiology Report Generation
items.abstract_600: AI-driven models have demonstrated significant potential in automating radiology report generation for chest X-rays. However, there is no standardized benchmark for objectively evaluating their performance. To address this, we present ReXrank, https://rexrank.ai, a public leaderboard and challenge for assessing AI-powered radiology report generation. items.abstract_600: Abstract We develop a framework for difference-in-differences designs with staggered treatment adoption and heterogeneous causal effects. We show that conventional regression-based estimators fail to provide unbiased estimates of relevant estimands absent strong restrictions on treatment-effect homogeneity. items.title: RAID: A Shared Benchmark for Robust Evaluation of Machine-Generated Text Detectors
items.abstract_600: Many commercial and open-source models claim to detect machine-generated text with extremely high accuracy (99% or more). items.abstract_600: Post-disaster communication remains a critical challenge in emergency response, as traditional reporting channels are often fragmented, overloaded, and slow, causing delays in situational awareness, triage, and coordination. items.abstract_600: Defining the reasoning boundaries and ensuring the reliability of Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) remains a critical challenge. items.abstract_600: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being explored as a tool to support pharmacometric modeling, particularly in addressing the coding challenges associated with NONMEM.
